title: Audit logging: emit OptimizeConfigChange events with gating results + redaction and payload limits
author: Felix Schneider
description: Title: Audit logging: emit OptimizeConfigChange events with gating results + redaction and payload limits Context: We need audit-quality evidence that Optimize configuration changes are gated by quality guardrails before being applied, and we need to ensure the event payload is safe (PII) and bounded (size) for downstream sinks (internal pipeline + SIEM export). This PR implements the OptimizeConfigChange audit event emission, includes the guardrails gating summary (pass/fail/timeout/override) and adds redaction + payload size limiting consistent with Security guidance. This unblocks customer asks like SUP-18544 ("prove eval checks ran before cost changes") and aligns with the control-plane gating enforcement work in ENG-3913/ENG-3918. What’s in this PR: 1) New/updated audit event fields (OptimizeConfigChange) - Adds guardrails_gating block to the OptimizeConfigChange audit event with: gating_state: PASS | FAIL | TIMEOUT | ERROR | SKIPPED | OVERRIDDEN gating_run_id (stable id from eval runner job) policy_version (GuardrailPolicy version id) threshold_bundle_version (version string; resolves to threshold schema version) prompt_set_revision (string; if multiple suites, includes a summary and per-suite revisions) eval_suites (comma-separated suite ids in payload; see size limiting) summary_metrics (small set of pre-agreed metrics; numeric values rounded; no raw per-prompt data) failure_reasons (machine-readable codes + short human text) override (if present): requested_by, approved_by, justification_hash, justification_preview (redacted + truncated), override_ticket (Linear/Jira id when present) - Includes config_delta summary: optimization_type (quantization/batching/caching/routing) + normalized before/after markers (no raw customer prompt content, no full routing rules). - Adds linkage fields: tenant_id, project_id, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), actor (user id / service principal), request_id, and apply_operation_id to correlate to API requests and downstream traces. 2) Redaction rules (PII-safe) - Introduces a centralized redaction helper for audit payloads applied to OptimizeConfigChange prior to emission. - Explicitly redacts: any prompt text, model outputs, tool arguments, structured output examples, customer-provided "notes" fields, and any freeform justification text beyond a preview. - Applies allowlist-based logging for gating metrics: only metrics defined in GuardrailsMetricAllowlist are included; all unknown metric keys are dropped (prevents accidental leakage via metric labels). - Normalizes IDs: hashing of prompt_set_id when the source is customer-supplied and not yet whitelisted for logging. 3) Payload size limits + deterministic truncation - Adds a hard payload limit of 16KB for audit events (post-redaction). If over limit: - Drops low-priority fields in a deterministic order (per-suite details first, then long lists like eval_suites, then failure reasons beyond N). - Truncates long strings with "…" and records <field>_truncated=true markers (flat booleans represented as "true"/"false" in the internal event map; serialized consistently). - Adds a payload_digest (sha256 of the fully redacted, pre-truncated payload) to preserve integrity for investigations while still respecting size constraints. - Adds tests to ensure the truncation order is stable (prevents flapping / non-deterministic audit payloads). 4) Emission points + behavior - Emits OptimizeConfigChange on Optimize apply completion in the control plane (not the Console) with a final outcome (APPLIED or BLOCKED) and gating_state. - Ensures we still emit an event when gating fails/timeouts (BLOCKED + gating_state=FAIL/TIMEOUT) so security/compliance can see attempted changes. - For async apply workflows, emits a "requested" event (OptimizeConfigChangeRequested) only when configured behind a flag; default in this PR is to emit only the final OptimizeConfigChange to avoid double-counting until downstream dashboards are updated. 5) Tests + validation - Unit tests: redaction allowlist, truncation determinism, payload_digest stability, and "no raw prompt" invariants. - Integration tests (mock audit sink): verifies we include gating_run_id/policy_version and do not exceed 16KB. - Manual verification: exercised apply flow in staging with (a) PASS (b) FAIL (c) TIMEOUT mocked by eval runner; confirmed event is present in audit stream and is searchable by request_id + gating_run_id. Files/areas changed (high level): - control-plane/optimize/apply/ApplyHandler.ts: add audit emission after gating decision + apply result - control-plane/audit/events/OptimizeConfigChange.ts: event schema mapping + field normalization - control-plane/audit/redaction/redact.ts: new allowlist-based redaction helpers - control-plane/audit/limits/payloadLimit.ts: size enforcement + truncation strategy + digest - control-plane/audit/tests/optimizeConfigChange.test.ts: schema + redaction + size tests - docs/internal/audit-events.md: updates to OptimizeConfigChange field definitions (internal only) Example (redacted) event payload (illustrative): OptimizeConfigChange { tenant_id=ten_..., actor=user_..., optimization_type=quantization, outcome=BLOCKED, gating_state=FAIL, gating_run_id=grun_01JFD..., policy_version=gpol_v12, threshold_bundle_version=2024-12-guardrails-rc3, eval_suites=[quant_safety_v2, format_compliance_v1], summary_metrics="task_success:0.84->0.79; format_valid:0.98->0.91", failure_reasons="FORMAT_DRIFT:format_valid delta -0.07 exceeds -0.02" } Notes / non-goals: - This PR does not change the audit event export mechanism to customer-owned SIEM; it ensures the event payload is compliant and bounded so it can be exported safely. - This PR intentionally does not include per-prompt artifacts or links to raw eval outputs; those remain in eval artifact storage with separate access controls. Rollout plan: - Guarded behind feature flag: audit.optimize_config_change_v2 (default ON in staging, OFF in prod until next release train). - Once enabled in prod, we will monitor: event volume, payload truncation rate, and any redaction false positives (missing required compliance fields). - Security/Compliance sign-off required before enabling for Private deployments with custom audit sinks. Checklist: - [x] Added tests for redaction + size limits - [x] Verified event emitted for PASS/FAIL/TIMEOUT - [x] Confirmed no prompts/outputs leak in payload - [x] Added deterministic truncation to avoid flapping - [x] Updated internal audit event docs Review notes: - Please pay attention to the truncation drop order and the allowlist for metric names. We should keep it aligned with Applied ML’s metric taxonomy so we don’t accidentally drop key signals (but we also must not allow arbitrary metric keys).
commits: audit: add OptimizeConfigChange v2 schema including gating summary
audit: implement allowlist redaction for optimize audit payloads
audit: add payload size limit + deterministic truncation + sha256 digest
optimize: emit OptimizeConfigChange after apply completion (pass/fail/timeout)
tests: add no-raw-prompt invariants and size-limit coverage
docs: update internal audit event reference for OptimizeConfigChange
review_conversation: Naomi Feldman (Security/RBAC): Can we guarantee no customer-provided freeform strings end up in the audit payload? Specifically: override justification + any prompt set names. Also, do we have a hard bound for payload size to satisfy SIEM exporters?

Felix Schneider (author): Yes. Justification is stored separately; in the audit event we emit (1) justification_hash (sha256) and (2) a 120-char preview that is run through the same redact() pipeline (emails/phones/IPs masked) and then truncated. Prompt set *names* are not emitted; we emit prompt_set_revision and a hashed prompt_set_id for non-Redwood-owned sets. Payload is hard limited to 16KB post-redaction; if over, we drop fields deterministically and mark truncation flags + compute payload_digest.

Marcus Lin (Security design reviewer): +1 on allowlist. Please ensure metric keys are strictly controlled; otherwise labels can be used as a covert channel. Also, can we avoid logging raw exception strings in failure_reasons?

Felix Schneider (author): Metric keys are now allowlisted in metricAllowlist.ts; unknown keys are dropped. For failure_reasons we emit (code, short_message) where short_message is mapped from known enums; we do not log raw stack traces. Internal errors are normalized to ERROR_INTERNAL or ERROR_EVAL_RUNNER with a short canned string.
Ethan Park (Control plane): Emission point looks good. Question: do we emit on BLOCKED cases as well? Compliance asked for visibility into attempted changes.

Felix Schneider (author): Yes — outcome is APPLIED or BLOCKED, always emitted after decision. For TIMEOUT/ERROR we also emit BLOCKED unless tenant tier is configured for manual approval (that logic is in apply handler; the event records gating_state=TIMEOUT and outcome=BLOCKED).
Kevin Osei (Audit export/SIEM): 16KB cap is fine. Please add a stable digest so we can correlate truncated payloads with the source in case downstream truncates again.
Felix Schneider (author): Added payload_digest computed from the fully redacted pre-truncation payload; also added unit tests for stability.

Naomi Feldman: Requested change: Please rename justification_preview to override_justification_preview to avoid confusion with other events and to make it explicit in schema. Also add a test that proves prompt/output strings are dropped even if accidentally passed in from upstream.
Felix Schneider (author): Done in 6f2c9a1. Added explicit invariant tests that fail if fields match /prompt|completion|tool_args/ keys or if any string exceeds 2KB without truncation markers.
Marcus Lin: Approved after changes. Thanks for being strict on allowlists.
Kevin Osei: Approved. Please coordinate with me before enabling the flag in prod so we can confirm exporter mappings.
